mistakes.cause: iRacing multiplies the paint by the metal, so a dark paint under metal turns dark; flat mirror metal also reflects a cloudy sky

articles.title: What Shokker Paint Booth makes (Getting Started)
articles.summary: Shokker Paint Booth makes iRacing spec-map liveries .
articles.what: Shokker Paint Booth makes iRacing spec-map liveries . Every car in iRacing reads a paint file (the colors) and a spec map (the instructions for how light behaves on the surface — what's chrome, what's matte, what's candy, what catches fire when you roll past a corner worker). SPB builds both, automatically, from the finishes you choose. Three honest things, so we start on the same page: It's a spec-map tool, not a painting app.

deep.heading: More detail
deep.body: You're not airbrushing flames pixel by pixel — you're telling light what to do. Think material designer, not Photoshop. There's no spinning 3D car preview. We can't render iRacing's cars and we won't fake it. You design here, render, and look at it in iRacing , where it counts. Your car has no "shininess" slider in real life either. Light just does stuff to chrome that it doesn't do to suede. The spec map is how you boss the light around.

deep.body: That's the whole trick. Beta, reminder #1 This is an early build. We shipped it because the only way to find the weird stuff is to let real painters drive it. Expect updates often — that's a feature of beta, not a bug in it.

articles.title: The spec map: the one idea that makes everything click
articles.summary: iRacing lights your car using three channels.
articles.what: iRacing lights your car using three channels. You never hand-edit them — you pick a finish and SPB writes all three. But knowing they exist explains why a finish looks the way it does. M · RED CHANNEL Metallic Is this surface metal or not? Cranks the difference between a flake-loaded chrome and a flat painted panel. R · GREEN CHANNEL Roughness Mirror-smooth to dead matte and everything between.

deep.heading: More detail
deep.body: Low roughness = that wet, glassy look. High = it eats light. CC · BLUE CHANNEL Clearcoat The glossy coat on top. articles.title: Zones: telling Shokker where
articles.summary: A zone is a region of the car defined by color.
articles.what: A zone is a region of the car defined by color. Point at a color, SPB grabs everything that matches, and now you can dress that region however you like. Tolerance — how fuzzy the match is. Low = that exact shade. High = the whole neighborhood. Fixes 90% of "it grabbed the wrong stuff." Hard Edge — crisp boundaries instead of soft blends. Multi-color zones — stack several source colors into one zone when they should wear the same finish.
